sources.entry: visual-explainer by nicobailon - Agent skill and plugin that turns complex terminal output into styled HTML pages or slide decks for diagrams, diff reviews, plan audits, data tables, and project recaps. Generates self-contained browser-readable artifacts with Mermaid diagrams, responsive layouts, themes, and sharing commands.

summary.one_liner: An agent skill that turns complex terminal output (diagrams, diff reviews, plans, tables, recaps) into self-contained, styled HTML pages or slide decks that open in a browser.
keywords: turn output into a web page
summary.what_it_does: The skill tells a coding agent to render complex explanations as a single self-contained HTML file, written to ~/.agent/diagrams/ by default and opened in a browser, instead of ASCII art or wide terminal tables. Built-in commands cover web diagrams, visual implementation plans, slide decks, narrated MP4 videos, visual diff reviews, plan checks against the codebase, project recaps, side-by-side option comparisons, and document fact-checking against code. Pages are figure-first and use hand-drawn inline SVG diagrams, with Mermaid available on request. Optional features include an 11-palette theme and font picker, a --slides flag on commands, and a best-effort static PPTX exporter. The README also describes a local stdio MCP server and a Pi native tool that prepare and render pages. Installation paths are documented for many agent harnesses, including Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, and Pi.
use_cases: draw a diagram of a system or auth flow without ASCII art
review a git diff visually with architecture comparison
check an implementation plan against the codebase
turn a large comparison table into a readable page
generate a slide deck from a technical topic
get a mental model recap of a project after time away
build a narrated MP4 explainer video
notable: Output is a self-contained HTML file with no build step, viewable in any browser
Diagrams are hand-drawn inline SVG that match the page theme and can step through a process
Theme and font picker with 11 palettes such as Dracula, Nord, and Gruvbox
Local stdio MCP server that writes only to a configured output directory and does not start an HTTP listener
Installs across many harnesses: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, Pi, and others
caveats: PPTX export is best-effort and static; animations, navigation, and live Mermaid/Chart.js rendering are not preserved, so the HTML deck is the source of truth
Video export needs ffmpeg, Chrome, and playwright-core installed separately
Auto-opening the page depends on the harness, browser access, and sandbox rules
The README states results vary by model capability
